draft.title: Pronumerals on both sides
card: Some equations have a pronumeral on both sides, such as \(5x - 3 = 2x + 9\). First collect the pronumeral terms on one side.
Add or subtract the same term on both sides. To remove \(2x\) from the right, subtract \(2x\) from both sides: \(3x - 3 = 9\).
Now solve as usual. Add 3 to both sides: \(3x = 12\). Divide both sides by 3: \(x = 4\).
Check by substituting into both sides. Left: \(5(4) - 3 = 17\). Right: \(2(4) + 9 = 17\). The sides match, so \(x = 4\) is correct.
draft.remember: Do the same to both sides: move the pronumeral terms together, then solve.

a.q: To solve \(7x + 2 = 3x + 18\), which step collects the pronumeral terms on one side?
opts: Subtract \(3x\) from the left side only
a.why: Subtracting \(3x\) from both sides removes it from the right and gives \(4x + 2 = 18\). Adding \(3x\) would give \(10x\) on the left and still leave \(6x\) on the right, so the terms would not be collected.
a.clue: Remove the smaller pronumeral term from both sides.

b.q: Mia solves \(6x - 5 = 2x + 11\). What is the value of \(x\)?
b.why: Subtract \(2x\) from both sides: \(4x - 5 = 11\). Add 5: \(4x = 16\). Divide by 4: \(x = 4\). Check: \(6(4) - 5 = 19\) and \(2(4) + 11 = 19\). The answer \(x = 1.5\) comes from subtracting 5 instead of adding it.
b.clue: Check your answer in both sides of the equation.
